chunks: And what Zayd ibn al-Jahm al-Hilali narrated, he said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman and marries his son to her daughter, and he said: If the daughter is already married to him before he marries her, there is no harm. The way to understand these two reports is to interpret them as a type of dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (haram), because the causes of prohibition are known, and nothing from among them is present here. And that which indicates that the intended meaning of both is a type of dislike is according to what we have previously established.

key_terms.أَسْبَابَ الْحَظْرِ: The causes or reasons that lead to prohibition
key_terms.الكَرَاهِيَةِ: Dislike or mild disapproval in Islamic jurisprudence, distinct from prohibition
key_terms.الْبِنْتُ لَهَا: The daughter being already married (to the father)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry a woman and his son to her daughter simultaneously?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of simultaneous intermarriage between a father and son with a mother and daughter, ruling it permissible provided the daughter is already married to the father. Shaykh al-Tusi notes that conflicting reports are reconciled by interpreting them as indicating *karahah* (dislike/preference) rather than *haram* (prohibition), since no specific impediment exists. This reflects the Shia principle of distinguishing between absolute prohibition and recommended dislike in marital contracts.
